source_locator: R644: p. 76, 86; R643: listing under the 6th Panzer Army heading; R243: table of 1944, 15 December row
current_activity: LXVII Corps (Corps Monschau) attacks north and south of Monschau with two divisions
notes: Event date: CMH Ardennes ch. 5 p. 76: "the LXVII Corps (General der Infanterie Otto Hitzfeld) had only two infantry divisions, the 326th and 246th Volks Grenadier"; p. 86: "his LXVII Corps ( Corps Monschau )"; Nafziger 944GLAA (15 December 1944): "LXVII Corps: General der Infanterie Otto Hitzfeld"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, LXVII. Armeekorps, table 1944: 15 December, 6. Panzerarmee, Heeresgruppe B, "Hürtgenwald / Malmedy". Event definition: the opening of the offensive on 16 December. Event support: three source families (CMH, Nafziger, Lexikon). Location: Monschau with a precision of 10 km, the town the corps was named for and attacked around. Location approximate: a town point. Location support: CMH names Monschau and Höfen; the NAF listing and the Lexikon row name the army. Commander: General der Infanterie Otto Hitzfeld. Opponents: US V Corps (99th Infantry Division, 2nd Infantry Division).

location_qualifier: corps sector east of the Ondenval defile covering St. Vith
current_activity: Model transfers the LXVII Corps (Hitzfeld) to the Sixth Panzer Army on 17 January to unify command near St. Vith
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 2 p. 46: "Field Marshal Model at Army Group B on the 17th unified command in the sector by transferring Hitzfeld's LXVII Corps to Dietrich's Sixth Panzer Army"; p. 45: "the LXVII Corps (General der Infanterie Otto Hitzfeld) of Zangen's Fifteenth Army". Event definition: the transfer on 17 January. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Saint-Vith with a precision of 25 km, the town whose approaches the corps defended; no headquarters place is named. Location approximate: the town of St. Vith for a corps sector. Location support: CMH names the Ondenval defile and St. Vith as the sector. Commander: General der Infanterie Otto Hitzfeld. Opponents: US V Corps and XVIII Airborne Corps. Context: CMH p. 45 calls the corps part of the Fifteenth Army in the days just before 17 January, which differs from the existing relation CR0688 (Sixth Panzer Army from 16 December); the relation is left as it stands and the difference is an open question in the batch report.

current_activity: LXVII Corps (Hitzfeld) is told at 0100 on 7 March that the Remagen bridgehead is its responsibility
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 11 p. 210: "at 0100 on 7 March, at the same time Zangen ordered the LXVII Corps to counterattack the spout of the funnel leading to Remagen, he also told Hitzfeld the Remagen bridgehead was then the responsibility of the LXVII Corps". Event definition: the order at 0100 on 7 March. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Remagen with a precision of 3 km, the town of Remagen, the bridgehead named for the corps responsibility. Location approximate: a town point for the bridgehead. Location support: CMH names Remagen. Commander: General der Infanterie Otto Hitzfeld. Opponents: US III Corps.

location_qualifier: eastern end of the assigned line
current_activity: Hitzfeld's LXVII Corps is told to build a line from the Harz east to Halle while the rest of the army enters the Harz
notes: Event date: CMH The Last Offensive ch. 17 p. 389: "the best of General Hitzfeld's Eleventh Army, the LXVII Corps"; p. 391: "All contingents of Lucht's Eleventh Army except Hitzfeld's LXVII Corps tried to reach the mountains on the 10th"; "building a line from the Harz eastward to Halle". Event definition: the order given on or just before 10 April; CMH says all contingents except the LXVII Corps tried to reach the mountains on the 10th. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Halle (Saale), Sachsen-Anhalt with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: Halle stands for the eastern end of a line from the Harz to Halle; the corps headquarters is not placed. Location support: CMH names Halle as the eastern end of the line. Commander: General der Infanterie Otto-Maximilian Hitzfeld. Opponents: US 3d Armored Division.
